'''Cuitlatec''', or '''Cuitlateco''', is an [[extinct language|extinct]] [[language isolate]] of [[Mexico]], formerly spoken by an [[indigenous peoples of Mexico|indigenous people]] known as [[Cuitlatec people|Cuitlatec]].

==Classification==
Cuitlatec has not been convincingly classified as belonging to any [[language family]].  It is believed to be a language isolate.  In their controversial classification of the [[indigenous languages of the Americas]], Greenberg and Ruhlen include Cuitlatec in an expanded [[Chibchan languages|Chibchan]] language family ([[Macro-Chibchan]]), along with a variety of other Mesoamerican and South American languages.<ref>{{Cite journal

==Geographic distribution==
Cuitlatec was spoken in the [[Mexican state|state]] of [[Guerrero]].  In the 16th century, the [[Relaciones geográficas]] recorded Cuitlatec spoken in [[Ajuchitlán]] and Tetela del Rio, while it was also known to be spoken along much of the [[Costa Grande]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Cline |first1=Howard F. |title=Handbook of Middle American Indians, Volume 12: Guide to Ethnohistorical Sources, Part One |date = 1972 |publisher=University of Texas Press |isbn=1477306803 |page=308}}</ref> By the 1930s, Cuitlatec was spoken only in [[San Miguel Totolapan]]. The last speaker of the language, Juana Can, is believed to have died in the 1960s.<ref name=Hern/> In 1979, only two elderly women, Florentina Celso and Apolonia Robles, were able to remember about fifty words of the language.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Valiñas Coalla|first1=Leopoldo|last2=Cortina Borja|first2=Mario|last3=Mireles Padilla|first3=Miguel|date=2010-03-11|title=Notas sobre el cuitlateco|url=http://www.revistas.unam.mx/index.php/antropologia/article/view/15915|journal=Anales de Antropología|language=es|volume=21|issue=1|doi=10.22201/iia.24486221e.1984.1.15915|doi-broken-date=11 July 2025 |issn=2448-6221}}</ref>

==Grammar==
Sentences generally follow [[subject–verb–object|SVO]] word order.  [[Adjective]]s precede the nouns they modify.
